acceptanceMatrix.condition: Gacha, login bonuses, payments, and in-game advertising are explicit required product systems in all affected canonical documents.
Monetization does not displace the cat-led hero-and-merchant fantasy; the battle, living tower, shops, and deliveries remain the first five-minute value proposition.
The gacha sells optional recruitable adventurer cats and/or alternate combat styles with clearly defined roles; it does not sell unknown mixed junk pools or required story access.
Mugi, Luna, Toto, Kohaku, and every role required to clear the first district have deterministic non-paid acquisition paths.
Every paid randomized purchase shows per-item or unambiguous type odds, pity progress, duplicate conversion, banner end rules, and draw history before purchase.
Complete-gacha and any reward that requires collecting a paid randomized combination are prohibited; duplicate progression is capped, disclosed, and not required for baseline usability.

Paid draws, premium balances, login claims, ad rewards, and entitlements are server-authoritative, idempotent, auditable, and impossible to mint through local clock, reload, replay, multiple tabs, or modified client code.
The wallet separates run coin, Dawn shard, free premium currency, paid premium currency, and non-currency tickets/entitlements; paid currency does not expire and all conversions are disclosed.
Web, iOS, and Android payment channels use a provider adapter with server receipt validation, webhook idempotency, restore, refund, revocation, and region-specific product availability.

The initial paid catalog is limited to premium-currency packs, a one-time starter pack, a monthly pass, cosmetic or style packs, and ad removal; each offer shows exact contents and value without fake discounts.
Login bonuses use server time, claim exactly once, do not reset a player's entire streak after a missed day, and include separate newcomer, monthly, and returner tracks.

Rewarded advertisements require explicit opt-in. Interstitials, if retained after UX review, appear only at natural breaks, have a strict frequency cap, and never interrupt battle, loading-before-action, gacha reveal, purchase, or save recovery.
Ad rewards are finite, disclosed, server-verified, and simulated as an economy persona. Ad removal disables forced/banner formats while leaving optional rewarded ads available by user choice.
Age rating, minors' purchase controls, consent, personalized-ad restrictions, privacy disclosures, inappropriate-ad reporting, and parental protections are explicit release gates.

The information architecture expands honestly from nine gameplay screens to twelve canonical screens: the existing S01-S09 plus S10 Recruit/Gacha, S11 Store/Ads, and S12 Login/Rewards/Inbox. Monetization is not hidden inside unrelated screens.
Save schema and account migration distinguish local gameplay state from server-owned wallet and entitlements, support guest-to-account linking, and prevent rollback or duplicate grants.

Balance validation expands to at least three gameplay builds multiplied by four monetization personas with 1,000 seeds each, plus a separate high-volume gacha-tail Monte Carlo and probability conformance suite.
The free-to-play no-ad persona can clear 100F within the accepted product time envelope; spending and ads accelerate or diversify but do not become a hidden mandatory gate.
Purchase, draw, login, ad, refund, and entitlement events have privacy-minimized analytics, customer-support lookup, immutable audit IDs, and reconciliation reports.

Independent critics separately attack monetization ethics and UX, probability/economy, platform policy and Japanese regulation, backend security and fraud, and mobile information density; unresolved P0/P1 must be zero before PASS.

failureConditions: Any paid draw or premium balance is generated client-side.
A story-critical first-district role is available only through paid randomness.
Odds, pity, duplicate conversion, or banner rules are hidden or ambiguous.
Complete-gacha or paid randomized combination rewards are introduced.
A missed login resets all accumulated monthly progress.
An ad interrupts active combat or appears before the action a user just selected.
Paid and free premium balances are merged without an auditable ledger.
A payment, refund, webhook, ad callback, or login claim can grant twice.
The nine-screen registry remains unchanged while three monetization surfaces are hidden elsewhere.
Step 2 starts before the expanded executable contract is sealed.
Any write targets a branch other than kimi.
